To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tachykin-1 receptor stimulation activates the transcription factor NF-kappabeta via a G(q) protein-dependent signaling pathway that involves PLC, calcium, Ras-Raf-MEK-Erk and proteasome activity in lung epithelial cell lines.
substance P, acting through the tachy-kinin-1 (neurokin-1) receptor, activates NF-kappaB through a G(q)- and phospholipase-C-dependent pathway that involves calcium, Ras, and Raf-1.
tachykin-1 receptor (Tac-1R) activation of G(q) is sufficient for NF-kB activation in lung epithelial A549 cells and is necessary for the proinflammatory actions of tachy-kinins in the lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the pro-inflammatory actions of tachykins.
the mechanisms that control the release of tachykirin peptides from sensory nerve terminals.
the mechanisms by which the neuropeptides substance P and neurokinin A stimulate the expression of proinflammatory genes in lung epithelial and endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP activates the Tacr1 in the epithelium and that this leads to activation of NFkappaB through a G(q)-mediated pathway.
the Tacr1 receptor is a member of the G protein-coupld receptor family of receptors that is capable of coupling to both the G(q)/G(11) and G(s)/G(i) families of G protein heterotrimers.

tachykin-1 receptor activation in lung epithelial cell results in NF-kappa B activation through a G(q)-coupled pathway that involves activation of phospholipase c, calcium, Ras/Raf-1/MEK/Erk and proteasome activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of NF-kB in the lung epithelium by tachykinergic nerve activation is mediated through a G(q) dependent pathway.
SP, acting through Tacr1, activates NF-kappaB by a G(q)- and G(s)-independent mechanism in A549 cells.

tachykinergic neurons in the respiratory tract can stimulate the production of proinflammatory cytokines in lung epithelial and inflammatory cells by activating the transcription factor NF-kB through a G(q)- and Ras-dependent signaling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tachykinine-1 receptor stimulation in lung epithelial cell activates NF-kappaB transcription factor via Gq-dependent pathway.
the activation of NF-kB is a mechanism by which the tachykirin-1 receptor, a G protein-couple receptor, stimulates inflammatory gene expression in lung cells.

tachykinergic nerves in the lung can stimulate the production of inflammatory mediators by lung epithelial cells, and that this effect is mediated by activation of G protein-coupling receptors on the lung epithelial cells.
